title: A generic Result wrapper for cache and APIs
hook: Returning T? from a cache Get mixes three stories: miss, stored empty, and fault. A small Result<T> (or a TryGet) makes the generic real in production instead of a textbook List<T>.

sections.heading: The production problem
sections.prose: Redis GET can miss. A session JSON can deserialize to a DTO whose claims are missing. An SQS payload can be well-formed JSON of the wrong type. If your API is SessionDto? Get(string key), a null means all of those. Interviewers who have shipped workers want a discriminated outcome. You can use bool TryGet<T> with [MaybeNullWhen(false)] (module 07 attributes) or a dedicated generic struct. Keep it in your domain; do not pull a 15-package Result library to look senior.

snippets.label: Result<T> for a Redis session lookup
snippets.explanation: Hit versus Miss versus Fault stay distinct. T is closed at the call site (SessionDto). Callers switch on Hit/Error instead of testing null three ways.

sections.heading: Design notes
sections.prose: Prefer a readonly struct to avoid allocating on the miss path. Do not constrain T to class unless you must; a cache of int counters should work. Found(T value) takes a non-nullable T so you do not store a “hit” of null. Fault carries a string or an exception type — keep it small. This is not a replacement for exceptions on programmer errors (ThrowIfNull on the key). It is for expected outcomes at an I/O boundary. Pattern matching on Result belongs with module 11; here the generic is the point.

sections.heading: When TryGet is enough
sections.prose: Dictionary.TryGetValue already is the BCL Result. Mirror it for Redis when you only need hit/miss: bool TryGet<T>(string key, [MaybeNullWhen(false)] out T value). Reach for CacheResult<T> when you have a third state (deserialize fault) you refuse to encode as miss. That choice is the senior sentence.

interviewTakeaways: A generic Result/TryGet separates miss, hit, and fault at cache and deserialize boundaries.
Unconstrained T? is a poor miss signal; attributes or a wrapper are clearer.
Keep the type small; do not hide ThrowIfNull for broken arguments inside Result.
commonPitfalls: Returning default! on miss and calling it a hit.
Making Result a mutable class with ten properties copied from an exception hierarchy.
Using exceptions for Redis misses in a hot 999-concurrency path.

jsTsCorrelations.note: { ok: true, value: T } | { ok: false, error: string } is the TS shape of CacheResult<T>. TS erases it; C# can keep a real struct.
